readerInvitation.closingInvitation: Begin with the introduction’s method and the example of the anti-consumption assistant. Then follow the chapter matching the obstacle your own project actually encounters. The funding chapters expose the difference between missing evidence and a missing sponsor. The later chapters test how proposed solutions can preserve legitimate refusal. This book suits builders, policy readers, and writers imagining plausible institutional futures. Its full cases teach you to distinguish a weak idea from an incompatible selection environment. That is a concrete gain: a better diagnosis before another proposal repeats the same failure.
